1_Learning_Objective.Title: 🎯 The "Why Are We Learning This?" (Learning Objective)
1_Learning_Objective.Content: The goal is to help your child observe a picture carefully, spot details, and use simple English words to describe what people or animals are doing (action words) and what objects are there (naming words).

2_The_Hook.Title: 🪝 The Hook (How to start the conversation)
2_The_Hook.Content: While sitting in the living room, suddenly say: **'Freeze! If I took a picture of this room right now, what are three things I would see in the photo?'** Let them guess. Then say, **'Books have pictures that tell whole stories. Let's be detectives and find the hidden stories in our book!'**

Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'When we look at a picture, first we find the THINGS. Trees, dogs, boys, girls. Point with your magic finger and name what you see!'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: Open a storybook or family photo album. Play a rapid-fire game of pointing and naming things (e.g., 'Tree!', 'Car!', 'Grandpa!').

Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'Now let's see what everyone is DOING. Are they running? Eating? Sleeping? Let's look for the action.'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: Act out simple actions at home (drink water, jump, read). Ask your child, 'What am I doing?' Let them say the action.

Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'Let's stick the thing and the action together! Instead of saying just *Boy* or *Run*, we say *The boy is running*.'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: Have your child roll a ball. Ask them to describe it in a full sentence: 'The ball is rolling.' or 'I am throwing the ball.'

4_Common_Stumbling_Blocks.Title: 🚧 Common Stumbling Blocks (What to watch out for)
4_Common_Stumbling_Blocks.Content:
Kids will naturally just point and say one word (e.g., 'Dog'). 
*   **How to clarify:** Gently stretch their sentence. If they say 'Dog', you say, 'Yes! What is the dog doing? The dog is... sitting!' Encourage them to repeat the full phrase.

Questions.Question: Look at this picture. Can you point to the cat?
What is the cat doing in the picture?
Questions.Expected_Answer: The cat is sleeping / drinking milk.

Questions.Question: Can you put it together and tell me a story about the cat in one sentence?
Questions.Expected_Answer: The cat is drinking milk from the bowl.

Activities.Name: 1. I Spy With My Little Eye
Activities.Description: Play 'I Spy' in whatever room you are in. 'I spy something green that is growing.' Let them guess (a plant!). Then let them take a turn.

Activities.Name: 2. The Freeze Dance Picture
Activities.Description: Play music and dance. When you stop the music, shout 'Freeze!' Take a mental picture and describe what each other is doing. 'You are standing on one leg!'

Activities.Name: 3. Magazine Detectives
Activities.Description: Take an old newspaper or magazine. Give them a pencil and ask them to circle three people who are smiling, or two people who are walking.

Activities.Name: 4. Family Photo Story
Activities.Description: Look at a favorite picture on your phone. Have your child tell you what is happening in the photo using a full sentence (e.g., 'Daddy is eating cake!').
